archetype: Naya Dinosaur typal battlecruiser, v2: still a linear critical-mass ramp deck compressed into one commander combat trigger — but the seven verification-gated swaps moved a VERIFIED enrage ping web maindeck, giving the deck a second, combat-independent engine and a bracket-report floor of 4 whose verified reality argues 3.

role_assignment.default_role: Quiet ramp player for turns 1-6 — a control POSTURE, not a control deck (strategy:whos-the-beatdown). Unchanged from v1, with one upgrade: the ping web (stack 005) gives the deck a mid-game VALUE line before the pivot — every Dinosaur ETB with Forerunner of the Empire out converts into exile-removal, ramp, draw, and a token, so the deflection turns (strategy:multiplayer.threat-deflection) are no longer dead turns. Experienced tables will still discount the posture; now they will also be right to.
role_assignment.pivot_trigger: Unchanged: castable Gishath + a held protection instant + an opponent who cannot profitably block or answer (strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window). New secondary acceleration: Selvala or Regal Behemoth online can drag the pivot forward two-plus turns off the naked 7.97 mean — Selvala taps for X = greatest power among your creatures, which a 5/5 Polyraptor or Trapjaw Tyrant makes 5+. The web itself is a pivot hedge: if the Gishath turn never comes, the deck still accrues.

engines.engine: Engine one, VERIFIED: combat damage to a player reveals that many cards, free-rolling every Dinosaur among them onto the battlefield. Stack 001 (checker pass) confirms the cascade on a real board: one 7-damage connection = five new bodies, three Garruk's Uprising draws, and a Pantlaza discover at X=6 — with the verified sequencing lesson that Pantlaza's once-per-turn discover must be stacked to resolve BEFORE the Regisaur Alpha token enters. 34 threat:body entries (deck-facts) keep the reveal dense. Note: Forerunner of the Empire is a Human Soldier — the reveal never free-rolls the web's hub.
engines.evidence: verified stack 001 (checker pass); deck-facts roles histogram; oracle text

engines.piece: Enrage ping web (Forerunner of the Empire + Ranging Raptors + Trapjaw Tyrant + Ripjaw Raptor + Polyraptor)
engines.engine: Engine two, VERIFIED, and the headline of v2: stack 005 (checker pass) resolves one optional Forerunner ping on the exact post-swap board — a single Dinosaur ETB yields an opponent's 1/1 dead to SBAs, their 3/3 exiled under Trapjaw Tyrant, a Ripjaw draw, a Ranging Raptors tapped Forest, and a Polyraptor copy token whose own ETB RE-ARMS Forerunner with a genuinely new optional trigger. Cost: 1 damage marked on each of your creatures, all surviving, clearing at cleanup. Goldfish v3: enrage engine 72.6% drawn by t6 (up from 49% in v1). This is combat-independent value the wrath-rebuild can lean on (strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math) — but every link routes through Forerunner, a 1/3 Human Soldier outside ALL the deck's tribal protection: Temple Altisaur's prevention names other Dinosaurs, the typal lands' mana names Dinosaurs, Gishath's reveal free-rolls Dinosaurs, and Forerunner's own sweep hits it (it took 1 of 3 in stack 005 and died to its own third sweep in stack 003).
engines.evidence: verified stack 005 (checker pass); verified stack 003; goldfish_metrics.json enrage target 0.726 by t6; oracle text

engines.piece: Polyraptor + Forerunner of the Empire (the bounded burst)
engines.engine: VERIFIED BOUNDED, and the crux of the bracket conversation: the combo DB tags this pairing a two-card infinite (produces 'Infinite creature tokens' etc., mana_value_needed 0), and that tag alone forces the computed floor from 3 to 4 (bracket_report driver 'two_card_infinite'). Stack 003 (checker pass) verified the actual ceiling: maximum SEVEN Polyraptor tokens, reached only by DECLINING one intermediate 'you may' trigger (yes-to-everything caps at six), self-terminating when Forerunner dies to its own third sweep, safely stoppable at every link. Bounded, controllable, not infinite. The engine does not consult passing stacks (known limitation, hapatra precedent), so the report honestly presents floor 4 while the verified-reality argument is 3 — see key_tensions.
engines.evidence: verified stack 003 (checker pass); bracket_report.json drivers; data/combo_details.json record via deck-facts

engines.piece: One-sided sweep package (Blasphemous Act + Temple Altisaur + Wrathful Raptors — now ALL maindeck)
engines.engine: VERIFIED: stack 004 (checker pass) resolves the full line, with one correction of scale the frame must carry — Temple Altisaur is not 'another Dinosaur' to itself, eats its own 13 and dies, but its death still converts to a 13-point Wrathful Raptors redirect via last known information; your other Dinosaurs are each dealt exactly 1 and survive; SBAs clear the opponents' creatures BEFORE redirect targets are chosen, so all 16 redirect damage goes at a player (40 to 10, not lethal from 26). Ripjaw draws a card. In v1 Wrathful Raptors was benched; the swap block put the whole package maindeck. This is the deck's asymmetric answer to the go-wide tables it cannot race, and it manufactures the self-damage the enrage shell wants (v1's 'bring your own damage' tension, partially resolved).
engines.evidence: verified stack 004 (checker pass); oracle text; cards.json is_sideboard flags

engines.piece: Big-mana acceleration (Selvala, Heart of the Wilds + Regal Behemoth, both new maindeck)
engines.engine: The swap block's direct attack on the 7.969 mean cast turn: Selvala taps for X = greatest power among your creatures ({G},{T}), which the deck's 5/5s make 5+ from the mid-game; Regal Behemoth grants monarch and adds an extra mana on every land tap while you hold the crown. The goldfish explicitly models neither (stated assumptions: reducers/rituals/extra draw unmodeled), so 7.969 / 8.3%-by-t6 is the floor of the problem, not the expectation — but treat acceleration claims as projection, not simulation. Monarch is also a threat-deflection cost: it paints the crown-holder (strategy:multiplayer.threat-deflection).

Carries over from v1 unchanged: once-per-turn discover X = entering Dinosaur's toughness, no combat and no 8 mana required — the engine that keeps working the turn after a wrath. Now verified in situ by stack 001, including the once-per-turn sequencing trap (discover before the token enters, or lose the big X).

engines.piece: Cheat/reducer layer (Urza's Incubator, Belbe's Portal, Monster Manual, Descendants' Path, Huatli, Poet of Unity)
engines.engine: Carries over: goldfish v2 'Cost reducer or cheat-into-play drawn' 56.2% by t6 (mean turn 3.0). The deck-facts restricted-mana trap stands: Unclaimed Territory is spells-only and cannot activate Portal or Manual; Secluded Courtyard pays only creature-source abilities, which Portal/Manual are not — both typal lands accelerate the cast plan, never the cheat plan.
engines.evidence: goldfish_metrics.json targets; deck-facts notes on restricted mana; oracle text

engines.piece: Ramp shell (21 lands + ramp:land 5 + rocks 5 + dorks 3 + cost-reduction 3)
engines.engine: Ramp/fixing drawn 86.9% by t6 (mean turn 2.0, up from 82%), yet land-drop hit rate falls to 52.6% by t6 and mean available mana is 5.486 at t6 — the deck ramps early then rides rocks and dorks, the exact profile a mid-game sweeper punishes on both board and mana (strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math). 21 lands remains far below the ~40% baseline (strategy:deckbuilding.curve); Selvala and Behemoth deepen the nonland-mana dependency the sweeper preys on. Wrath exposure is UNCHANGED by the swaps.
engines.evidence: goldfish_metrics.json (ramp 0.869 by t6, land-drop 0.526 t6, mean mana 5.486 t6); deck-facts roles/curve

engines.piece: Protection suite (Heroic Intervention, Flawless Maneuver, Boros Charm, Akroma's Will, Eerie Interlude)
engines.engine: Carries over: 48.5% held by t6 per goldfish v3 — the swing-turn insurance for an engine hub that costs 8 plus tax (strategy:multiplayer.commander-insurance). One new duty the suite inherits: the board-wide instants (Maneuver, Will, Charm, Intervention) are the ONLY shields that cover Forerunner of the Empire — the web's hub is invisible to every tribal protection layer, so the swing-turn insurance is now also the engine insurance.
engines.evidence: oracle text; goldfish_metrics.json protection target 0.485 by t6

engines.piece: Draw engines (Garruk's Uprising, Curious Altisaur, Bonehoard Dracosaur, Etali, Primal Storm + Ripjaw Raptor via the web)
engines.engine: Carries over, upgraded: the cheapest-rebuild package after a wrath (strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math), now with Ripjaw Raptor's enrage draw verified live in both stacks 004 and 005 — the web makes card draw a side effect of every ping.
engines.evidence: oracle text; deck-facts roles (draw:engine 4, draw:impulse 2); verified stacks 004, 005

candidate_missing_lines.title: Marauding Raptor + Polyraptor: mandatory whole-table draw (REFUTATION — why the eighth swap was declined)
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: combo_details lists it as a win ('Infinite creature tokens' etc.) alongside 'Draw the game'. Stack 002 (checker pass) settled it: every trigger is mandatory, 2 damage never kills a fresh 5/5 token, the deck has no loop-breaker, and if no opponent intervenes CR 732.4/104.4b end the game in a DRAW for all players. A liability, not a wincon — Marauding Raptor stays benched (HISTORY.md: deliberately NOT promoted), and any future promotion requires adding a free sacrifice outlet or instant-speed self-removal first.

candidate_missing_lines.title: Wrathful Raptors × the Forerunner ping web: does redirection starve the enrage engine?
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Both are now maindeck, and their verified stacks never share a board: stack 005's ping web resolved WITHOUT Wrathful Raptors out; stack 004 shows Wrathful converting damage dealt to your Dinosaurs into redirects. Whether a Forerunner ping with Wrathful on the battlefield still marks damage on your Dinosaurs (and so still triggers Ranging/Ripjaw/Polyraptor enrage) or is turned into redirects (free reach, dead engine) turns entirely on Wrathful's exact wording — unresolved rules work this frame will not guess at.

candidate_missing_lines.title: Selvala/Behemoth fast-cast: Gishath by turn 5
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Selvala for X≥5 plus lands plausibly casts Gishath two-plus turns ahead of the 7.969 goldfish mean, and the goldfish's own assumptions exclude both cards. But no artifact quantifies it — the claim needs either a goldfish model extension or a worked sequencing scenario before the manual may state a number.

matchup_frames.vs_sweeper_control: Still the worst frame, now with a real consolation: the Gishath board remains one sweeper from zero and 'deploy in waves' remains structurally unavailable — the trigger IS the wave (strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math). Swing only with a board-wide protection instant held, into the tapped-out turn (strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window, strategy:multiplayer.commander-insurance). What changed: the ping web is a rebuild engine the wrath does not fully erase the value of — Trapjaw's exile undoes on its death (the hostage returns), but Ranging Raptors' lands and Ripjaw's draws are banked. Priority one after a wrath: redeploy Forerunner plus any one Dinosaur, because the web restarts at two cards while the Gishath plan restarts at 8-plus-tax.
matchup_frames.vs_stax: Carries over: taxes hit the 8-drop hardest; fight over enablers, not payoffs (strategy:critical-mass), mulligan toward the cheat layer (strategy:mulligans.engine-hands), remember Unclaimed Territory cannot activate Portal or Manual. New: the ping web is the deck's best under-stax posture — it runs on creature ETBs, not activations or big casts, and Selvala's single activation makes big mana tax-resilient. Spot removal (6 slots) still goes to the piece that turns off the cheat layer specifically (strategy:threat-assessment.answer-economy).
matchup_frames.vs_aggro: Carries over with a verified upgrade: the deck owns the long game (strategy:whos-the-beatdown.metagame-clock) and takes the control role — but the one-sided sweep is no longer hypothetical. Stack 004 verifies Blasphemous Act under Temple Altisaur + Wrathful Raptors as a board-clearing, 16-damage-redirecting catch-up play whose only friendly casualty is Temple Altisaur itself. Trapjaw Tyrant plus one ping is verified repeatable exile removal (stack 005) for the one creature that actually races (strategy:threat-assessment). Turn the corner immediately on stabilizing (strategy:combat-math.racing).
matchup_frames.vs_combo: Still the bad seat and materially unchanged by the swaps: no counterspells in Naya, 6 spot / 2 sweeper interaction, clock starting turns 6-8. Per strategy:threat-assessment.answer-economy, spend removal on enablers now rather than banking it, and take the beatdown role regardless of posture (strategy:whos-the-beatdown). The web speeds the clock at the margin (tokens, exile on their blockers) but adds zero pieces of interaction; the honest plan is still racing.

distribution_notes: 65 nonland spells over 21 lands, curve mode 3 (18 entries); ~40% of the deck still makes or reduces mana beneath a 34-body typal top. Goldfish v3 (10k iterations, seed 42, sha fb3507e3b705): ramp/fixing 86.9% by t6 (mean 2.0, up from 82%); enrage engine 72.6% by t6 (up from 49% — the single largest swap-block effect); Dinosaur payoff 62.3%; cheat/reducer 56.2%; connection kit 51.4%; protection 48.5%. Commander mean cast 7.969 (was 7.932), 8.3% by t6, 55.3% of games never cast him by t10 — marginally worse on paper than v1 because the simulator models neither Selvala nor Behemoth nor the reducers (stated assumption); the naked number remains the honest ceiling of the problem, not the expectation. Land-drop hit rate 52.6% at t6, mean mana 5.486. The v3 mana-base tune (+Windswept Heath +Commercial District +Arctic Treeline for three basics) raises the Forest-typed card count 9→11, feeding the deck's Forest-fetching effects (Nature's Lore, Skyshroud Claim, Krosan Verge, and Windswept Heath itself). Pips comfortable: G 54 total (38 cards) against source targets 36/36/36 with land sources G11/R12/W9 — the colour weight rides the 13 nonland producers. Role coverage 93.0%; the six no-role cards are taxonomy holes, not dead slots. Deck-facts synergy note: 0 intra-deck edges — the global top-10 shortlist says nothing about internal fit.
key_tensions: THE FLOOR CONVERSATION (report says 4, verified reality argues 3): the computed floor moved 3→4 solely on the two_card_infinite driver — the combo DB tags Polyraptor + Forerunner as an infinite assembling at MV ≤6. Stack 003 (checker pass) verified the pairing as BOUNDED: max 7 tokens, requiring a declined trigger to even reach 7, self-terminating when Forerunner dies to its own sweep, stoppable at every link. The bracket engine does not consult passing stacks (known limitation, hapatra precedent — the engine already distrusts DB bracket tags in the other direction). Frame it exactly as strategy:deckbuilding.power-level frames brackets: contents give a floor, never a verdict, and brackets are 'a tool to guide pregame conversations'. The report should present floor 4; the pilot should open Rule 0 with the verified fact — the DB calls one pairing infinite, the stack shows it caps at 7 tokens and stops itself — and let the table land on 3. That conversation IS the bracket system working (strategy:deckbuilding.power-level.barometers: a verified line beats a tag).

THE WEB HANGS ON A HUMAN: every verified ping line routes through Forerunner of the Empire, a 1/3 Human Soldier standing outside all tribal protection — Temple Altisaur shields only other Dinosaurs, Secluded Courtyard/Unclaimed Territory mana names Dinosaurs, Gishath's reveal free-rolls only Dinosaurs, Descendants' Path misses it, and its own sweep damages it (verified: 1 of 3 in stack 005; dead to its own third sweep in stack 003). Only the board-wide protection instants (48.5% held by t6) cover it. Opponents who read the board kill the 1/3 first and cheaply (strategy:threat-assessment).

WRATH EXPOSURE UNCHANGED: the swaps added zero resilience to the sweeper problem — 21 lands, nonland mana that dies to board wipes, one wave of payoff. The web softens the rebuild but does not change the math of the swing turn (strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math).
overall_assessment: V2 is the fair battlecruiser that grew a verified second engine. The deck still plays the critical-mass game (strategy:critical-mass): seven turns of deflection-postured ramp (strategy:multiplayer.threat-deflection) into one combo-timed pivot (strategy:pivot-point, strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window) — but where v1's enrage shell was a benched promise, v2's is checker-verified fact on the exact post-swap board: one optional ping converts any Dinosaur ETB into exile-removal, ramp, draw, and a fresh 5/5 that re-arms the trigger (stack 005), with a bounded 7-token burst mode (stack 003) and a verified one-sided table sweep (stack 004) beside it. The swap block also bought acceleration (Selvala, Regal Behemoth) against a naked 7.97 mean cast the goldfish cannot see past, and it correctly declined the one trap: Marauding Raptor's pairing is a verified whole-table draw (stack 002), a liability the deck cannot exit. The frame's honest core is the bracket tension: the report computes floor 4 off a DB tag that stack 003 refuted in substance — the deck should be PRESENTED at 4 and ARGUED at 3, out loud, before the game, which is precisely what strategy:deckbuilding.power-level says brackets are for. Its structural weaknesses are the same two as v1, now sharper: everything still folds to a well-timed wrath, and the new engine's every line runs through a 1/3 Human the deck's entire tribal apparatus ignores.
gaps: Still no strategy section on typal/tribal construction (critical-mass of a creature type, typal-land tradeoffs, off-tribe hub creatures like Forerunner) — v2 needed it even more than v1 did.

Still no section on self-damage/enrage-style engines (creature damage as a resource); nearest hits are life-total sections. This deck now has a VERIFIED such engine and no doctrine to cite for piloting it.
Still no section on cheat-into-play / cost-cheating as an archetype axis.
Still no section on top-of-library stacking as setup discipline (Congregation at Dawn / Worldly Tutor into the reveal).

New and now load-bearing: no section on reconciling computed bracket signals with verified-bounded lines — when a combo DB tag and a checker-passed stack disagree, what does the pregame conversation owe the table? strategy:deckbuilding.power-level gestures at it ('contents give a floor, never a verdict') but the verified-refutation case deserves its own treatment; this deck and hapatra are now two precedents.
